guidance: A clear-sky receive-chain figure of merit: antenna gain minus 10 log10 of the system noise temperature. It does not model rain or atmospheric noise, availability, interference or the rest of the link budget.
method: The receive figure of merit is G/T = G - 10 log10(T_sys) in dB(K^-1), with G the antenna gain and T_sys the system noise temperature. The feed between the antenna and the LNA is a lossy two-port: with loss L in dB its loss ratio is alpha = 10^(L/10) > 1, it delivers T_a / alpha of the antenna noise and adds (1 - 1/alpha) T_phys of its own at physical temperature T_phys, so T_sys = T_a/alpha + (1 - 1/alpha) T_phys + T_R referred to the LNA input. T_R is the LNA noise temperature, converted from its noise figure as T_R = 290 (10^(NF/10) - 1) at the 290 K standard reference. The effective receive gain is G - L, and the page reports G/T at the receiving port; the antenna-port form G - 10 log10(alpha T_sys) reduces to (G - L) - 10 log10(T_sys), so the figure is independent of the reference plane. Only the clear-sky chain is modelled: the atmospheric and precipitation term of the recommendation, antenna spillover, interference and any availability margin are excluded, and the antenna temperature entered is the clear-sky sky-plus-ground temperature at the antenna terminals. Inputs are plain numbers in dBi, K and dB; a loss of 0 dB and a noise figure of 0 dB are accepted, and an all-zero chain is refused because G/T would be undefined. The arithmetic runs in the browser and nothing is sent or stored.
